title: The legacy treatment entity, its plan timers and its DP04 extract are split across three services, and no source states what the plan-timer data model holds on the S2 side once the clock moves to rwb-case
source: Legacy RWB-E2-004 (04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epic 2 Story Files v5/RWB E2 004 Treatment entity and plan timers data model v2.md, sections 1, 4, 11, 12, 13); FSD S2 TDR, settlement and deed in lieu v3 A2.10; TSD S2 TDR, settlement and deed in lieu v2 T2, T3.0, T3.1, T3.3, T5.3, T-A.1; _work/msr/context/S2.md (ownership rows: tables 1 treatment, jobs 0, events 1 EV-10, workflows 1 TreatmentWorkflow); Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-01, DP-09, DP-10, DP-17 and §R5.7; RWB-P3-E2004-CON sections 1, 2, 4 and 12
section: 1 Story; 2 Business rationale; 4 Flow; 7 Acceptance criteria AC2, AC5, AC8; 8 Business rules BR3 and BR7; 9 State transitions; 11 Data; 12.6; 12.7; 13 Solution plan; 15 Screens and states; 19 Out of scope
description: One combined row for the split. (1) The legacy story holds one treatment table, one timer table, one Quartz job and one nightly DP04 extract inside one module, and its AC2, AC12 and AC14 assert timer rows, TimerDue and a single TimerScheduler port; the context pack gives S2 exactly one owned table (treatment), no job and one event, and gives rwb-case the timer, so the timer entity, its unique plan index and the TimerDue event are not S2's deliverable (ASM-B2-S2-014-1). (2) No source states which plan facts the S2 row must carry for the case clock to be built: TSD S2 T3.1 lists first_due_date, installments, installment_amount, installments_paid and installment_shortfall but states no rule for who writes them or when, so the working read is that S2 holds them and publishes them on TreatmentApproved. (3) No source states the state vocabulary of the treatment row or its moves: the legacy BR8 lists APPROVED, BOOKED, RUNNING, BROKEN, COMPLETED and CANCELED for the data product, and nothing states how the record reaches them, so section 9 derives the moves from the case and payment signals. (4) The legacy AC1 to AC14 and their sixteen test cases are assigned by the split plan to RWB-P3-E2004-APP as the primary slice; this story therefore carries no legacy criterion, and the legacy traceability of REQ-CHO-006, REQ-CHO-007 and REQ-RDF-014 is completed there. (5) The DP04 treatment copy is no longer this module's extract: DP-17 and ASM-A6-tables-14 give it to rwb-source-data as a read-only copy built from events, which is why no job, no extract operation and no data-lake output appears in this story.
evidence: Context pack S2 ownership rows ('Tables (1) treatment', 'Jobs (0) None', 'Events (1) EV-10'); legacy RWB-E2-004 sections 12 ('JOB-05 Timer check ... JOB-15 Reporting extract') and 13 ('adds timer.treatment_id uuid with index ix_timer_treatment_id ... ix_timer_plan_due'); TSD S2 v2 T3.1 (DF-TRT-009, DF-TRT-029 and DF-TRT-031 to DF-TRT-033 only) and T5.3 (one event, TreatmentApproved); RWB-P3-E2004-CON sections 1, 2 and 12.6 (TimerScheduler, JOB-05 and TimerDue retired; timer row is a projection behind the case timers operation); split_plan.json slice RWB-P3-E2004-APP acs AC1 to AC14
area: S2 data model and timer ownership across S2, P3 and P1
owner_role: Solution architect with the data owner of rwb-treatment and the owners of rwb-case and rwb-source-data
proposed: Hold the treatment entity and the plan facts on one table in rwb_treatment, publish them on rwb.treatment.TreatmentApproved.v1, derive the treatment state from the case and payment signals, keep no timer table, no Quartz job, no TimerDue topic and no extract, and leave the fourteen legacy criteria and their sixteen test cases with RWB-P3-E2004-APP.

title: The parameters and reference-data operation names, the contract fake set, the field-level type of the event payload and the guard that limits a case to one running plan are not published for rwb-treatment
source: TSD S2 TDR, settlement and deed in lieu v2 T3.1, T3.2, T5.2, T6.1 and appendix T-A.1; FSD S2 TDR, settlement and deed in lieu v3 A2.10.3 and A2.1.3.1; Template and Rules v1 §R7.2 section 12 and §R9; RWB-P3-E2004-CON sections 3, 4 and 12.2
section: 3 Preconditions; 7 Acceptance criteria AC1, AC3, AC4, AC7, AC9; 8 Business rules BR10; 11 Data; 12.1; 12.2; 12.3; 12.8; 12.9; 13 Solution plan
description: One combined row for the contract slice. (1) No source names the operation of the parameters read or of the reference-data read that this service calls for CURE_PERIOD_DAYS, plan.warn-days and the seven lists: TSD S2 T5.2 states only that the calls go through the published interfaces of P3 and P4, and no path or media type is published for either. (2) No source states the field-level types, lengths and required flags of the TreatmentApproved payload; the eight members are named by RWB-P3-E2004-CON 12.3 at member level only. (3) No source states whether a case may hold more than one treatment in state RUNNING at a time; the legacy guard was a unique index on the timer table for one due date, and with the timer gone the guard has to be restated on the treatment row. (4) No source publishes a fake set or a consumer list for the treatment write and read, so the fakes of section 12.8 are generated from this document. (5) TSD S2 marks treatment columns as required only for seven fields and gives no column-level nullability for the plan facts, so the not-null set of section 13 is a working read.
evidence: TSD S2 v2 T3.1 (Required column: Yes for DF-TRT-001, 002, 004, 005, 006 and 032 only), T3.2 (list members without a version) and T5.2; FSD S2 v3 A2.10.3.1 (R-RES-25, no payload shape); RWB-P3-E2004-CON 12.3 (payload named at member level) and 12.2 (the S2 treatment read only)
area: S2 contract artefact and data-model constraints
owner_role: Contract owner of rwb-treatment with the parameters and reference-data owner of rwb-case
proposed: Name the two consumed operations, the member-level types of the event payload and the fake set in the service contract document at major version 1, and state the one-running-plan guard on the treatment row as a partial unique index; treat the nullability set and the guard as the working read of this gap until the document is frozen.
